rules.title: Stream over imperative loops only when it reads better
rules.what: Use streams where they clarify (filter/map/collect over collections), keep imperative loops where order, early exit or checked resources matter; never use parallelStream for I/O-bound work.
rules.why: parallelStream uses the shared ForkJoinPool for I/O-bound work: it blocks the common pool that everything else in the JVM depends on, and gains nothing on network waits.
rules.how: Sequential streams for clarity; explicit executors for parallel I/O; measured parallelism only for CPU-bound work with enough items.

patterns.note: parallelStream; verify the pipeline is CPU-bound and the data volume justifies it.

verify.how: Throughput measured sequential vs parallel on the real workload; common-pool contention checked.

limits: Some CPU-bound workloads do gain; the measurement is the verdict, the default is no.

rules.title: Try-with-resources everywhere
rules.what: Every Closeable (streams, connections, statements, files) is opened in try-with-resources; no manual close paths that an exception can skip.
rules.why: A leaked connection pool under load is a production outage in slow motion: the error path is the common path, and manual close on it is where resources go missing.
rules.how: try (var conn = ds.getConnection(); var ps = conn.prepareStatement(sql)) { ... } - the language construct makes the release unconditional.

patterns.note: Connection assigned outside try-with-resources; verify closure on all paths.

verify.how: Fault-injection test: pool usage returns to baseline after failures; no leaked connections in pool metrics.

rules.title: Lazy or batched JPA access
rules.what: JPA access avoids N+1: fetch joins or entity graphs for traversed relations, batched IN queries for collections, projections (DTO) over full entities where only fields are read.
rules.why: A lazy relation traversed in a loop issues one query per row; a full entity where three fields are read hydrates the whole graph per row. Both multiply silently with data.
rules.how: JOIN FETCH / @EntityGraph for accessed relations, IN-batching for collections, constructor projections for read paths; verify with hibernate query logging.

patterns.note: Relation traversal inside a loop; candidate N+1 with lazy relations.

verify.how: Hibernate statistics: query count constant as row count grows.

rules.title: Bound the JVM to the container
rules.what: JVM flags match the container's CPU and memory limits (MaxRAMPercentage), GC chosen for the workload and measured; no unbounded heap in a container.
rules.why: A JVM sized for a bare-metal machine inside a 512 MB container gets OOM-killed on the first peak; one sized correctly stays flat and avoids the swap spiral.
rules.how: -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75 (or explicit -Xmx), container-aware GC (Serial/G1/ZGC by profile), startup flags under version control, GC logs reviewed.

patterns.note: Very large fixed heap; verify it matches the container limit.

verify.how: Container memory profile under load: RSS within limit, no OOM kills, GC pauses within SLA.

rules.title: No reflection on hot paths
rules.what: Reflection, dynamic proxies and annotation scanning are kept off measured hot paths; the framework's start-up scope, not the request path.
rules.why: Reflection per request costs class metadata lookups and boxing on every call, and hides the actual work from profilers.
rules.how: Resolve reflection targets at startup, cache Method handles, use generated accessors on hot paths.

patterns.note: Reflective lookup; candidate if reachable from a request handler.

verify.how: Profile shows reflective lookup not in the top functions of the request path.

limits: Framework internals use reflection legitimately; the rule targets application code on hot paths.

rules.title: Batch writes in bounded transactions
rules.what: Write entities and JDBC rows in batches (saveAll with hibernate.jdbc.batch_size, addBatch/executeBatch) inside bounded transactions; set a fetch size on large reads.
rules.why: One save or commit per row is one round trip per row; an unbounded transaction holds locks and undo for the whole run.
rules.how: spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.jdbc.batch_size=50, flush()/clear() every N entities, JdbcTemplate.batchUpdate, setFetchSize on streaming reads.

patterns.note: Write call inside a loop: one round trip per row.

verify.how: Integration test counts statements: proportional to batches, not rows.

rules.title: StringBuilder in loops, parameterised logs
rules.what: Build strings in loops with StringBuilder, and log with placeholders (log.debug("x={}", x)) instead of concatenation.
rules.why: += on a String allocates at every iteration; a concatenated log message is built even when the level is disabled.
rules.how: StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(); SLF4J placeholders; guard expensive arguments with isDebugEnabled().

patterns.note: Concatenated log message; placeholders defer the formatting.

verify.how: No String += in loops; log calls use placeholders.

rules.title: Bounded caches, not static maps
rules.what: Cache through a bounded, expiring cache (Caffeine, Spring Cache with a spec) rather than a static Map that only grows.
rules.why: A static HashMap used as a cache keeps every entry until the JVM restarts: heap growth, longer GC pauses, eventually OOM.

patterns.note: Static map named as a cache; check bound and expiry.

verify.how: Every cache has a maximum size and an expiry.

rules.title: Scheduled tasks justified, not polling
rules.what: @Scheduled jobs run at a justified frequency and never stand in for an event; prefer messages or change notifications.
rules.why: A high-frequency scheduled task queries for rare changes around the clock, spending CPU and database capacity for nothing.
rules.how: Trigger from the write (application events, a broker, CDC); otherwise widen fixedDelay/cron and document why.

patterns.note: Schedule under 10 s; check it is not polling for an event.

verify.how: Each schedule's interval is documented and matches the data's real change rate.
